title: QBR - Quantum Labs - Health & Usage Review
summary: Quarterly business review focused on usage and cost trends (tokens/month up 42% YoY), p95 latency regressions on inference for long-context models, and roadmap alignment for 2027. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send cost-optimizer recommendations, SAML/SSO guide, and schedule a dedicated performance benchmark; customer to scope a pilot for Dedicated capacity for their peak inference workloads.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-20
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Rachel Liu (Head of ML, Quantum Labs), Mark Patel (Platform Eng), Aisha Khan (CTO)

[00:00:00] Sofia: hey everyone, thanks for making time today, uh this is our QBR slash health check for q4, quick agenda  usage, costs, reliability, then roadmap and next steps. Daniel's gonna lead the perf bits.
[00:00:18] Rachel: sounds good, thanks Sofia. we mainly want to understand the cost jump and that p95 spike we saw last month.
[00:00:25] Mark: and we wanna see if Dedicated makes sense for our peak. our infra team is cautious about networking changes.
[00:00:32] Daniel: great, i'll start with the reliability snapshot and then we can dig into config-level stuff. quick note, apologies if the transcript mis-says some product names  sometimes the call transcriber flips "redwood" to "reedwood".

[00:00:45] Daniel: so for the last 90 days, tokens per month are up about 42%  you moved from roughly 1.8B to 2.55B tokens, cost is up ~38% month over month in Dec because of two things: longer average sequence lengths (we saw avg seq length go from 320 to 480) and a 12% rise in inference volume. that compounded with some cold-cache tail calls.
[00:01:10] Rachel: yeah we added the multi-turn summarization flow and longer contexts for the research assistant. those prompts were longer.
[00:01:18] Sofia: does that line up with the billing export you saw? the token model mix changed?
[00:01:23] Rachel: slightly  we moved 18% of calls from the base model to the large long-context model mid-November per our A/B.

[00:01:30] Daniel: on latency p95  we observed a regression from ~220ms to ~410ms for the long-context variant during peak windows (14:00-18:00 UTC). p99 also moved from ~780ms to ~1.1s. Root causes look like transient KV-cache misses and larger batching queuing effect when sequence lengths vary a lot.
[00:01:53] Mark: that matches our traces  you'll see more queuing when small and huge seqs mix. can we prioritize per-route batching?
[00:02:01] Daniel: absolutely, we recommend route-level batching and dynamic batching thresholds; i flagged a config that reduces max-batch for the long-context route to avoid head-of-line blocking. i'll share exact values.

[00:02:12] Sofia: on the cost side we had a couple levers: quantization profile, caching prefixes for the assistant, and routing some workloads to cheaper model variants during non-critical windows. have you tried the cache TTL increases?
[00:02:24] Rachel: we increased TTL for session-level prefixes last week; it helped but we still have a lot of unique research queries.
[00:02:30] Sofia: ok, we'll combine prefix caching with intelligent reroute for best-effort queries so quality-sensitive calls stay on the long-context model.

[00:02:39] Aisha: curious about Dedicated  what are the clear cost inflection points vs hosted? we're not ready to commit to fixed capacity without seeing predictable ROI.
[00:02:48] Daniel: logical  Dedicated shines when you have sustained high throughput and need lower tail latencies. for your numbers, if you keep >2B tokens/month with high p95 sensitivity, Dedicated with reserved capacity gives better unit economics and predictable latencies, especially for long-context models. i'll add a modeled TCO slide.
[00:03:06] Mark: network concerns  peering and egress. we'll need the VPC checklist.
[00:03:11] Sofia: yes, we'll send the VPC/peering checklist and a sample network diagram.

[00:03:18] Daniel: on security, you mentioned SAML/SSO and KMS integration last quarter. status?
[00:03:22] Rachel: SSO is in place for our non-prod; we need guidance for enterprise SAML and KMS for key rotation.
[00:03:28] Sofia: i'll send the SAML guide and our KMS integration doc. also we'll include audit log retention options (SOC2 compatible).

[00:03:36] Mark: also compliance  we're in the procurement loop with InfoSec, so any compliance artifacts help.
[00:03:40] Sofia: yes, we'll attach SOC2 and ISO summaries plus a short compliance checklist.

[00:03:46] Daniel: back to perf  i'd like to propose a 2-hour benchmark where we run your representative prompts at scaled QPS. we can isolate dedupe/caching, run with and without quantization, and measure p50/p95/p99 and cost delta. gives a clear comparison Hosted vs Dedicated under your pattern.
[00:04:02] Rachel: sounds good. we'll provide prompt traces  they're the same we used for the A/B.

[00:04:08] Sofia: i've noted action items  daniel will prepare the benchmark spec, rachel will share 3 sets of prompt traces and billing exports, mark will review the VPC checklist. we'll set the benchmark week of Jan 4.

[00:04:20] Daniel: quick note on quantization: we've seen safe perf improvements with 4-bit quant on your model family, about 1.6x throughput and ~20-30% unit cost savings with marginal quality impact. we should run evals against your evaluation set for quality regressions.
[00:04:37] Rachel: we care about hallucination rates for the assistant; can't accept any significant delta.
[00:04:41] Daniel: agreed  we'll include quality metrics (ROUGE/accuracy) plus manual samples.

[00:04:47] Mark: is there an interim option  like burst capacity on Dedicated? we need to cover spikes but not over-commit.
[00:04:54] Daniel: yes, Dedicated offers burst pools and autoscaling policies. you can combine reserved base capacity with burst to handle spikes. cost modeling will show blended unit price.

[00:05:02] Aisha: timeline  procurement is ~6-8 weeks. can we run the pilot before the procurement completes?
[00:05:08] Sofia: yes, we often do a short pilot under a trial agreement to validate perf and cost before a formal contract. we'll include a legal point of contact.

[00:05:15] Rachel: any quick wins we can do now to reduce cost this month?
[00:05:18] Sofia: short term: 1) enable prefix caching for the session flows you mentioned, 2) route similarity-search type queries to smaller emb models, 3) enable quantization on low-risk backfills. we'll send a prioritized checklist.

[00:05:31] Daniel: also align batching strategies by route: set separate batch windows for the long-context summarizer vs short chat replies. small change, big latency win.

[00:05:40] Mark: great. about metrics and monitoring  can we get token-level cost breakdowns by route?
[00:05:45] Sofia: yes, Redwood Console can show per-route token cost and latency; we'll share a sample dashboard and give an invite for a cost dashboard view.

[00:05:52] Rachel: is there an eval harness for hallucination QA? we want to integrate into our CI.
[00:05:56] Daniel: Redwood's eval kit can do regression alerts against prompt sets; we'll share the repo and a short runbook.

[00:06:03] Aisha: can you include competitor notes? our procurement team asked how Redwood compares to Anthropic endpoints and self-hosting.
[00:06:09] Sofia: sure  we'll include a short comparison slide: Anthropic is strong on safety, Anthropic/OpenAI on model access, self-hosting gives more control but higher ops cost. Redwood focuses on production economics and unified tooling across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.

[00:06:20] Rachel: can we get a ballpark numbers doc for Dedicated TCO? even a spreadsheet to plug our numbers.
[00:06:25] Daniel: yes we'll share a TCO workbook and populate with your tokens and seq length.

[00:06:31] Sofia: recap of next steps  we'll send: cost optimizer deck, SAML/KMS docs, VPC checklist, perf benchmark spec, TCO spreadsheet and sample console dashboard. you'll share prompt traces and Nov/Dec billing. we'll schedule the perf run week of Jan 4. follow-up QBR in March.

[00:06:50] Mark: ok that's clear. thanks.
[00:06:52] Rachel: thank you both. appreciate the benchmarking offer.
[00:06:55] Aisha: thanks everyone.

[00:06:58] Sofia: thanks all, we'll circulate notes and notes links; expect the initial packet by Friday 12/24.

Meeting end.

Shared artifacts mentioned: cost deep-dive deck (drive link), VPC checklist, SAML guide, KMS integration doc, TCO spreadsheet, perf-benchmark spec (to be shared).

Transcription notes: occasional mis-labels (speaker overlap around 00:04:00), some proper nouns may be slightly off (eg "reedwood" vs "Redwood").
